newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch oil inspectors to send advance team to Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Dutch oil inspectors to send advance team to Iraq.

text.p: Dutch industrial inspectors Saybolt said on Thursday they will send an advance team of three monitors to Iraq when visas arrive.
"It could take about a week, but the moment we have the visas, we are ready...The advance team will go then," a Saybolt spokesman told Reuters.

The suspended United Nations/Iraqi oil-for-food deal signed on May 20 is eventually to allow Iraq to export oil -- $2 billion worth over six months -- for the first time since August 1990. Saybolt were appointed by the United Nations as monitors of the exports.
The Saybolt spokesman said the advance team will set up accommodation and facilities for a 14-strong oil inspection team and also make preliminary checks on Iraq's oil exporting capabilities.

On Wednesday, U.N. Under Secretary-General Chinmaya Gharekhan said minimum conditions do not yet exist in northern Iraq to implement the oil-for-food plan, but that the U.N. was hoping three monitors from Saybolt would go to Iraq soon.

Saybolt withdrew two technicians and a manager from Iraq at in early September after U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali postponed plans to implement the deal on safety fears after Iraqi troops entered Kurdish areas in northern Iraq at the end of August. --Philip Blenkinsop, Amsterdam Newsroom, +31 20 504 5000
